title_en: The Beauty of Traditional Korean Architecture
bibliographic_note: Author and English title read on PDF page 1; season appears in the printed running headings. Volume, issue, page range, and DOI were checked against the journal's article record. The publication-time publisher has not been separately established.
scope: Interpretive essay about traditional Korean architectural aesthetics and experience, framed through comparison with Western architecture. It is not a building survey or a settled account of all Korean architecture.
relevance: Offers a useful way to consider buildings, walls, courtyards, and bodily experience together when identifying evidence about palace settings and connections.

artifacts.verification_note: Checked %PDF- header, 21-page pypdf parse and readable native text; inspected complete Poppler renders of PDF pages 4 and 20. pypdf reported an incorrect startxref pointer but successfully read the original; no repair or rewriting was performed. Both supplied Beauty filenames have identical bytes and SHA-256, so only one original was retained. The Dropbox copy matches that original.

notes.statement: Kim argues that the relationships among buildings, walls, and courtyards should be considered together in discussing Korean architectural beauty. This makes spaces between structures and the experience of the setting relevant subjects of interpretation. The conclusion acknowledges difficulty in providing a clear-cut account of Korean architectural beauty.
notes.scope: An attributed aesthetic argument, including broad Korean/Western contrasts. It does not establish an arrangement, social practice, or universal trait for any particular palace building.
